analysis.title: DeskTalk - Macro radar: Unconvinced
key_insights: US equity benchmarks are recovering part of Thursday's selloff as tech rebounds partially. The NDX lost roughly $2.3tn of market value on Thursday, its largest single-day market value loss on record.

Sentiment in AI-linked names improved after Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa suggested existing data-center construction projects would be allowed to proceed while AI-related legislation is finalized.

Breadth is weak: more than 60% of SPX members are lower. Citi's cash equity desk sees inflows skewed toward Financials and Consumer Discretionary, with outflows in Info Tech, Industrials, Comm Services, Healthcare, Energy and Consumer Staples.

The tech rebound paused after reports that Microsoft (-1%) is scaling back plans to rent AI cloud capacity from Oracle (-2%), citing changing infrastructure requirements. The NDX (+1.2%) pared gains after being up more than 2%.
October payrolls came in at +165k, more than double expectations. USTs sold off initially and then settled, leaving yields modestly higher across the front end.
The desk describes a tug-of-war between dip-buying in tech after an extreme washout and a hawkish macro backdrop, leaving the market without conviction after peak event risk.

The dollar retreated from intraday highs but remains firm. CAD (-0.8%) underperformed after softer-than-expected employment data, and AUD fell to a seven-month low. The eFX desk sees flows skewed toward selling NZD, CAD and CHF, while NOK and MXN remain net buys.
Citi economists expect Tuesday's CPI to show core +0.19% MoM and headline +0.16% MoM, both below consensus. CPI is the next major macro catalyst.

tension_points.bull_case: Dip-buying in AI-linked tech after an extreme washout, helped by comments from Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa that existing data-center projects will proceed. The NDX was up more than 2% at one point.
tension_points.bear_case: Breadth is weak, with more than 60% of the SPX lower and outflows from Info Tech. The Microsoft-Oracle capacity report and a hawkish macro backdrop after strong payrolls add pressure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Tuesday's CPI report is named as the next major macro catalyst. The report does not state a specific level that would invalidate the rebound.
